To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Late Miocene palynofloral and faunal cycles within the Tripoli Formation and Calcare di Baso Formation in Sicily are related to basin isolation events resulting from thrust-related uplift.

the Tripoli and associated Calcare di Base formations of Sicily are characterized by a number of cycles, the origin of which was controlled by tectonic uplift, and the resulting isolation and restriction of basins.
The Tripoli and Calacre di Base Formations are Late Miocene in age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of palaeoenvironmental changes in the Tripoli and related Calcare di Base formations.
the Late Miocene of the Tripoli and related basins in central Sicily.
the recognition and correlation of the Late Miocene cyclicity in the Tripoli and related basins of central Sicily using a variety of sedimentological and faunal criteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the faunal and sedimentary cyclicity of the Tripoli and the Calcare di Base formations of the central and southern parts of Sicily were controlled by the interaction of two processes: 1) the partial evaporation of the Mediterranean sea, which was periodically replenished by inflows of Atlantic-derived water; 2) the development of a foreland basin and a perched basin, which were intermittently set into motion by the collision of the African plate onto a passive continental margin.
the Late Miocene sedimentary and faunal cyclicity in Sicily is the result of the combined effects of eustatic and tectonic controls.
the Late Miocene of the Tripoli and related basins in Sicily was controlled in a complex fashion by both eustatic and tectonic processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Late Miocene of Sicily is marked by a series of tectonically controlled, semi-isolated, marine basins, with a broad foreland and associated perched basin complex to the north and a series of perched basins to the south.
the Late Miocene of Sicily was a time when tectonic events and eustatic fluctuations combined to create a series of basins which were periodically isolated from open marine conditions.
a combination of eustatic and tectonic controls was responsible for the Late Miocence cyclicity in the Tripoli and associated basins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Late Miocene of Sicily was a time of complex tectonic evolution, with the Tripoli and associated Calcare di Base basin systems being intermittently isolated from open seas to the north by the development of submarine ridges and sills.
a combination of eustasy and tectonics controlled the cyclicity of the Tripoli and related Calcare di Base formations in Sicily.
it is not possible, under such a scenario of tectonic isolation, to distinguish between world eustatic events and local basin events, especially in the absence of a complete biota.
